text:
- chief complaint: positive hepatitis C antibody result found on routine screening during a physical; the patient feels fine but is anxious about the diagnosis.
- history of present illness: no prior hepatitis C diagnosis. Past intravenous drug use, clean for over fifteen years. Drinks one beer most days and smokes one to two cigarettes daily. Takes no medications. Family history of hypertension, diabetes, and depression. Labs show AST 39 (elevated), with normal ALT, albumin, and total bilirubin.
- physical examination: no distress or jaundice; regular rate and rhythm with grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur; lungs clear; abdomen soft with present bowel sounds and splenomegaly; no gait disturbance or edema.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: N/A (none reported; anxiety about the diagnosis only).
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: N/A.
- follow-up instructions: repeat hepatitis C antibody test; hepatitis C RNA, genotype, and liver elastography ultrasound to assess fibrosis; family doctor appointments to be arranged; return visit in three weeks.
